items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the
issuance of temporary retail permits; and to amend chapter 396 of the laws of
2010 amending the alcoholic beverage control law relating to liquidator's
permits and temporary retail permits, in relation to the effectiveness thereof
items.lawCode: Amd §97-a, ABC L; amd §5, Chap 396 of 2010
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9203

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the
issuance of temporary retail permits; and to amend chapter 396 of the
laws of 2010 amending the alcoholic beverage control law relating to
liquidator's permits and temporary retail permits, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would ease restrictions related to the issuance of temporary
retail permits.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 - Amends subdivision 3 of section 97-a of the alcoholic bever-
age control law, removing the need for there to have been an active
retailer at the location within the previous two years but maintains the
ban on issuing a permit if a location had a license previously
suspended, canceled, or revoked in the same timeframe.

Section 2 - Amends subdivision 4 of section 97-a of the alcoholic bever-
age control law, lengthening the 30-day extension period to 90 days with
the payment of a fee.

Section 3 - Amends subdivision 6 of section 97-a of the alcoholic bever-
age control law, allowing temporary retail permit holders to purchase
alcohol on credit.

Section 4 - Amends the alcoholic beverage control law to permanently
extend the SLA's authority to issue temporary retail permits.

Section 5 - Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Applicants for retail licenses to sell alcohol for on-premises consump-
tion typically rely on temporary permits issued by the SLA in order to
get their establishments up and running quicker as they await the issu-
ance of a full license, which often takes many months due to administra-
tive backlogs. Easing some of the limitations associated with being
awarded these permits will help more retailers get on firm footing in
accordance with their business plans.

 
FISCAL IMPACT ON THE STATE:

Potentially greater tax revenue.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill that incorporates the Executive's proposed FY 24 State Budget
language found within PPGG Part O.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that section
two of this act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall
have become a law.
